consent.title: Daily card
consent.description: A quick log of how you are doing, with a single purpose: helping your clinician follow your care and prepare sessions.
consent.who: Only the clinical team that cares for you sees what you log.
consent.realtime: Nobody monitors it in real time: what you write is read when preparing your sessions.
consent.optional: It's optional and you can stop at any time. What you've already logged may become part of your clinical record, which your clinician keeps for at least 5 years. Talk to them about it.
consent.accept: I understand and want to use the daily card.

support.title: Thank you for sharing how you are
support.description: If you are in danger right now, call your local emergency number. One of your answers shows you may be going through a very hard time, and you don't have to face this alone.
support.cvv: Call your local crisis line (in Brazil, 188 CVV, 24 h, free)
support.samu: In an emergency, call your local emergency number (in Brazil, 192 SAMU)
support.upa: Or go to the nearest emergency room.
support.professional: Your clinician will see this answer when they open the system, but not right away. If you can, also talk to someone you trust now.

instrument.title: Questionnaire: {name}
instrument.description: Your clinician added this questionnaire to your card. It takes about 2 minutes and helps track how you are doing over time.
instrument.credit: Screening scales, not tests or diagnoses. PHQ-9 and GAD-7: Drs. Robert L. Spitzer, Janet B. W. Williams, Kurt Kroenke and colleagues (free to use). WHO-5: Psychiatric Centre North Zealand and World Health Organization.

phq9.name: PHQ-9 (mood)
phq9.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
phq9.i1: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
phq9.i3: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
phq9.i4: Feeling tired or having little energy
phq9.i6: Feeling bad about yourself, or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
phq9.i7: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
phq9.i8: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed. Or the opposite: being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
phq9.i9: Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way

gad7.name: GAD-7 (anxiety)
gad7.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?
gad7.i1: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
gad7.i2: Not being able to stop or control worrying
gad7.i3: Worrying too much about different things
gad7.i5: Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
gad7.i7: Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen

who5.name: WHO-5 (well-being)
who5.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how much does each statement describe how you have been feeling?
who5.i1: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits
who5.i2: I have felt calm and relaxed
who5.i3: I have felt active and vigorous
who5.i4: I woke up feeling fresh and rested
who5.i5: My daily life has been filled with things that interest me
who5.o2: Less than half of the time
who5.o3: More than half of the time

pro.title: Daily card · {name}
pro.description: What the patient logged in the portal, with patterns to bring to the session. Association is not causation.

risk.title: An answer that needs attention
risk.description: On the PHQ-9, the patient endorsed item 9 (thoughts of being better off dead or of self-harm). Crisis contacts were shown to them. Assess risk and reach out according to your protocol.
risk.notePlaceholder: E.g. called the patient, assessed risk, booked an extra session.

pro.waitingConsent: The patient hasn't accepted the daily card in the portal yet. They will see the invitation next time they sign in.
pro.noPortal: The patient doesn't use the portal yet. Give access under "Open patient portal" so they can fill in the card.
pro.chartDescription: Dots: each day. Bold line: average of the last 7 logged days.
pro.empty: No entries in this period yet.

pixels.title: Mood in pixels ({weeks} weeks)
pixels.description: Each square is a day; the stronger the color, the better the mood.
pixels.aria: {count} of {total} days logged in recent weeks

patterns.title: Patterns
patterns.description: Associations in this period's data, to explore with the patient. They don't show causation.
patterns.sleepNotEnough: Sleep × mood: at least {min} days with both sleep and mood are needed ({count} so far).
patterns.sleep_none: Sleep × mood: no clear trend over {n} days (r = {r}).
patterns.sleep_weak: Sleep × mood: weak {direction} trend over {n} days (r = {r}).
patterns.sleep_moderate: Sleep × mood: moderate {direction} trend over {n} days (r = {r}).
patterns.sleep_strong: Sleep × mood: marked {direction} trend over {n} days (r = {r}). Worth exploring with the patient.
patterns.activity: {activity}: average mood {with} on the {days} days with it and {without} on days without.
patterns.activityNotEnough: Activities: at least {min} days with and {min} without each activity are needed to compare.

instruments.title: Screening scales
instruments.description: Scores and severity bands. They support clinical assessment, don't replace it, and are not psychological tests.
instruments.none: No answers yet. The questionnaire shows up in the portal when it's due.
instruments.off: No questionnaire turned on for this patient.
instruments.name: Questionnaire

setup.title: Customize the card
setup.description: Pick a template or adjust item by item. Fewer items usually means more entries.
setup.itemsHint: Mood is always on; the others are optional for the patient.
setup.questionsHint: E.g. "Did the 4-7-8 breathing?" (yes/no) or "How much did worry get in the way today?" (0 to 10). Custom questions don't trigger alerts: for risk, use the PHQ-9. Editing a question creates a new one; old answers are kept.
setup.instrumentsHint: They show up in the portal when due. The PHQ-9 includes the self-harm item: if answered above zero, the patient sees crisis contacts and you get an alert at the top of the app.
setup.riskAck: I understand Salutti does not monitor in real time and that I will assess PHQ-9 alerts according to my risk protocol.

errors.riskAckRequired: To turn on the PHQ-9, confirm you will assess alerts according to your risk protocol.

pro.chartAria: Mood chart: {count} days logged, average mood {avg} of 5, {low} low-mood days.
pro.printFooter: Patient self-report, generated by Salutti on {date}. Not a psychological document.
pro.templateNeedsAck: The PHQ-9 is added once you tick the risk protocol confirmation below and save.

revoke.title: Stop using the daily card
revoke.description: You'll no longer see the card or the questionnaires. What you've already logged stays with your clinician. You can come back any time.

alerts.description: an answer needs attention and has no recorded action.
